newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products end mostly higher on soy gains.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products end mostly higher on soy gains.

text.p: CBOT soy product futures ended mostly firmer but off earlier gains, led by soybeans on ideas tight U.S. supplies would pinch end-users, traders said.
The National Oilseed Processors Association on Thursday put weekly soybean crushings at roughly 25 million bushels, above expectations for 24.1 million to 24.9 million.

But domestic demand for soymeal continued strong and cash basis levels rose again on Friday, cash dealers said. They said they were seeing some "panic buying" in June and July positions as end-users tried to cover summer positions in anticipation of shortages.

The May soymeal contracts traded within $0.60 of the contract high of $2.97.00 before slipping off the highs as soybeans slipped. Contract highs were notched in the May and July soybean contracts near midday on ideas domestic and export demand were outstripping supply.
Traders also cited talk Sparks Companies, had issued a buy recommendation. But a Sparks spokesman said the company does not issue buy recommendations and he did not know the origin of the rumor.
Soymeal ended $3.90 to $1.00 per ton higher while soyoil closed 0.07 cent per lb higher to 0.11 cent lower.

On the day, funds were light buyers of soymeal and on both sides of soyoil. Refco Inc bought 100 lots each May, July, August, September and December soymeal, Produce Grain and Cargill Inc each bought 300 July and Merrill Lynch bought 400 July, pit sources said.
In soyoil, FIMAT Futures and Iowa Grain each bought 200 lots July while Rosenthal Collins sold 400 July. Cargill Inc bought 400 July.
Soymeal volume was estimated by CBOT at 25,000 contracts, compared with Thursday's actual volume of 20,615 lots. Soyoil volume was pegged at 19,000 lots, against Thursday's actual of 19,268 lots.
